On clear, calm nights, rural weather stations located in topographic depressions (frost hollows) pool cold air via katabatic drainage, whereas urban stations are sheltered, artificially inflating the apparent UHI gap.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If rural stations are carefully sited on flat, elevated terrain to avoid frost hollows, the UHI gap shrinks dramatically.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If wind speeds exceed the threshold for katabatic flow, cold air pooling does not occur.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If urban areas are also located in topographic basins, the measurement bias is neutralized.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Calm, clear nights are ideal for katabatic drainage, where cold, dense air flows downslope into rural valleys. If rural stations are sited in these hollows, they record anomalously low temperatures. Urban stations, situated on slightly elevated or rougher terrain, miss this pooling effect. The observed temperature gap is therefore a topographic artifact rather than a true thermal mass or radiative effect, and scales with local topography rather than urban form.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
